precepts.text: Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: give them warning from me. If the watchman does not warn the wicked from his wicked way, the wicked man dies in his iniquity, but his blood will I require at thine hand. As teachers we do not even have a choice: if we do not tell you what you are doing wrong, that blood is on our hands.
precepts.point: Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me. God commands the prophets to go and show the people their sinful deeds.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
In 2 Esdras 1:5 God commands the prophet: “Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds”. Go and show the people. Ezekiel was given the same charge: “get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” Whether they hear or forbear, our job is to go and tell them.

Then God tells him why: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.”

So as a prophet and teacher, it is required that we tell you what you are doing wrong, because if we don’t, we are liable to have that blood on our hands. It is not that we even have a choice. You call yourself a prophet, a teacher: your job is to go correct the people and help the brother.

That is why showing the people their sinful deeds is not hatred. Sometimes you have to show someone their shame, and that is God loving them too, because he could leave them right there to die and find out after death. It is our job to warn our people, to hopefully bring them to repentance, and when they come, to help them reform their ways. But they have to be willing to listen, and they cannot want correction for others while refusing it for themselves.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. If you see a brother in error and do not correct him, you hate your brother in your heart.
precepts.point: Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me. God commands the prophets to go and show the people their sinful deeds.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
If you see a brother that is in error and you don’t correct him, what does the scripture say you are? “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.”

If you see a brother in error and do not rebuke him, you hate your brother in your heart. Leaving sin upon him is not love; rebuking him in any wise is. So we have no choice but to tell our people what they are doing wrong, or we hate our brother in our heart.

That is the love behind 2 Esdras 1:5, “shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me”. Showing the people their sins is how you keep from hating them. And it goes both ways: when a brother comes to you and says this is wrong, hear it and learn, because you do not want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

precepts.text: I sent my servants the prophets, whom ye have slain and torn in pieces. Your houses will I give to a people that shall come, which not having heard of me yet shall believe me: that is us today.
precepts.point: They have thrown down thine altars and slain thy prophets, and I, even I only, am left. Israel's rulers killed the prophets who taught against them. The same people mock the purple and gold today.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
The Lord says it through Ezra: “I sent unto you my servants the prophets, whom ye have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, saith the Lord.” We were doing it to each other. We were killing the prophets of our own people, and he will require that blood.

“Thus saith the Almighty Lord, Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind doth stubble. And your children shall not be fruitful; for they have despised my commandment, and done the thing that is an evil before me.”

“Your houses will I give to a people that shall come; which not having heard of me yet shall believe me; to whom I have shewed no signs, yet they shall do that I have commanded them.” That is us today. We are born again.

Christ said the same in the parable of the vineyard: the husbandmen beat one servant, killed another and stoned another, and last of all killed the son, and the lord of the vineyard “will miserably destroy those wicked men, and will let out his vineyard unto other husbandmen”. The other husbandmen are us today, the people Ezra spoke of. “The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.”

precepts.text: The Most High destroyed many kings for Israel's sake; Pharaoh and all his power is the most popular account, and the Philistines knew it.
precepts.point: Still the Philistines rallied: be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you. They remembered serving Israel in the days of the Judges and refused to be slaves again, so they got ready to fight.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

precepts.why:
“Many kings have I destroyed for their sakes; Pharaoh with his servants and all his power have I smitten down.” The Most High destroyed many kings for Israel's sake. Pharaoh and all his power is the most popular account, and the Philistines knew it.

“And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, God is come into the camp.” They had never had to battle Israel with the ark of the covenant in the camp. They cried, “who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? these are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues in the wilderness.” The nations knew what the Most High did to Egypt. It was known throughout the earth, and to this day real history about what the Hebrews and their God did to the Egyptians is still taught on the other side of the earth. With the ark of the commandments among us, the nations understood they were dealing with something above a regular people.

Everything our people try to glory in about Kemet, the Lord smote down. The ten plagues humiliated ten plus different gods that the Egyptians served, all their power, all their magicians and wizards. Come out of that Kemet movement; the Lord destroyed it and said Egypt would not rise again as a power in the earth.

Still the Philistines rallied: “Be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you.” They remembered serving Israel in the days of the Judges and refused to be slaves again, so they got ready to fight.

precepts.text: A people who saw no signs would yet believe, showing the sign-gifts were not for today.
precepts.point: In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Your houses will I give to a people that shall come; which not having heard of me yet shall believe me; to whom I have shewed no signs, yet they shall do that I have commanded them.”

A people who saw no signs would yet believe and do what he commanded. The sign-gifts were not for today; the multitudes healed in Solomon's porch were for that time, to prove the power of the Most High, and the people that shall come believe without them.

points: Where are the benefits that I have done for you? When you cried in the wilderness he had pity and gave you manna, angels' bread. He cleaved the rock, covered you with leaves, divided a fruitful land, and cast out the Canaanites and Philistines before you. What shall I yet do more for you?

points: When you blasphemed at the river of the Amorites he did not give fire for it but made the water sweet. He fed you because you are special to him.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

points: What shall I do unto thee, O Jacob? Thou Judah wouldst not obey me. Seeing you have forsaken me, I will forsake you. He charged you to be over his people and lead them to him, and you take their money and walk in hypocrisy. Many stripes.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

points: And your children shall not be fruitful; for they have despised my commandment, and done the thing that is an evil before me. So these are the people that actually saw the miracles. I am just trying to fathom it in my mind, because some of them were us.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: Your houses will I give to a people that shall come; which not having heard of me yet shall believe me. So that is talking about people that have never heard of or seen the things that I have done — but they are going to believe everything I say.

To whom I have shewed no signs, yet they shall do that I have commanded them. I have not shown them any signs, no miracles, no healing, none of that — but they are going to do exactly what I say. That is us. That is you. You have not seen any miracles. That is why we listen to these pastors with all that healing and all that stuff. Man, they are not healing anybody, these dudes slapping them in the face with their jackets, blowing on them, spitting all over them. Over in Africa they are doing all types of crazy stuff, standing on women, people drinking gasoline, eating grass. People are just dying over there for stupidity. We lost our way.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: They have seen no prophets, yet they shall call their sins to remembrance, and acknowledge them. We have not seen any Peters, we have not seen any Pauls, we have not seen any Jameses. We have not seen these people — but we are going to call our sins to remembrance. You brothers are the prophets of God. You are the men that are going to teach God's word. Go out and teach these men, compel them, constrain them in by your words, by speaking God's words. That is what you are going to do.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: I wonder how the Most High really wants to deal with us. We are really not deserving. We are really not. But the Most High chose us, and it is what it is. He made a promise to us and he is upholding it. We have got to get it together. But listen — how great is it to take the most rebellious people on earth and make them the most righteous? Only the law, statutes and commandments can do that, and faith in Christ. That is it, to bring people into this state. That is why Christ was going around to the hoods. That is why we go to the hood — we are not going to Beverly Hills, we go to the hood where our people are. And that is who the Most High wants to teach the people: people that have been there before. That is why we have got people that were drug dealers, gang bangers, and those people are the best teachers. They are the ones that really go out there and put in the work. They use what they used in the world: I am going to push this truth like I was pushing weight on the corner.

Just imagine, when you have seen all those things you would think they would have a lot more faith, because they have seen the miracles, they have seen people getting healed, somebody that was blind now can see, a brother that was crippled now can walk and take up his bed. You would be like, this is the truth, I believe. But they were like, huh, whatever, that was cute, that was nice. He turned the water into wine — how do you lack faith at that time?

These people are going to have more faith than you, and they have never seen me. These people are willing to keep the commandments and they have never seen a prophet. That is you, brother and sister. These are the people out here going to go teach and put their life on the line. That is what we are doing right now. Our life is literally on the line when we go out and teach. Sisters, when your husband gets home you should be all over him because he made it home safe, because there is going to be a time that he might not come home. He might get put to death, and nine times out of ten it might not be the white man — it might be his own people that put him to death. The Bible talks about that. So we have got to make sure our election is sure, so when something like that happens we know where we are going. It is good to die in the truth. That is where I want to go. If I die I want to die in the truth. I do not want to be dead in the world.

I take to witness the grace of the people to come, whose little ones rejoice in gladness: and though they have not seen me with bodily eyes, yet in spirit they believe the thing that I say. We have not seen him with bodily eyes, but in spirit we believe. We believe it.
